evidence.observation:
New focused test added for a distinct command/config behavior: the coder configuration flag auto_commits=False. It reuses the file's established setup/action/assertion discipline exactly: GitTemporaryDirectory() -> git.Repo() -> committed fixture file -> InputOutput(yes=True) -> Coder.create(self.GPT35, "diff", io=io, fnames=[...], auto_commits=False) -> a mock_send closure that sets partial_response_content/partial_response_function_call -> coder.run(with_message="hi") -> assertions. Setup writes a committed file then leaves it dirty ('two
'); the action has the mocked model apply a SEARCH/REPLACE edit to 'three
'. Assertions are: coder.auto_commits is False, coder.dirty_commits is False (the derived config), coder.need_commit_before_edits is empty, the edit did land on disk (fname.read_text() == 'three
'), the repo still has exactly 1 commit (neither the dirty pre-commit nor the GPT edit commit happened), and coder.repo.get_commit_message was never called. auto_commits was previously exercised only at the argparse plumbing level in tests/basic/test_main.py, never at the coder behavior level, so this is a genuinely distinct behavior test.

Reference test whose discipline the new test mirrors. It is the canonical commit-behavior test in this file: GitTemporaryDirectory + git.Repo, InputOutput(yes=True), Coder.create(self.GPT35, "diff", io=io, fnames=[...]), a mock_send closure injecting a SEARCH/REPLACE diff, coder.repo.get_commit_message = MagicMock(), coder.run(with_message="hi"), then assertions on file content and len(list(repo.iter_commits(repo.active_branch.name))). The new test reuses this shape but flips the config so the commit count assertion demonstrates the flag's effect rather than the default path.

Configuration wiring under test: when auto_commits is falsy the constructor forces dirty_commits = False before assigning self.auto_commits and self.dirty_commits. This is the derived-config behavior the new test asserts directly (coder.auto_commits is False and coder.dirty_commits is False).

The guard clause `if not self.repo or not self.auto_commits or self.dry_run: return` is the runtime reason no GPT-edit commit occurs when auto_commits=False. Because repo.commit() is the only caller of repo.get_commit_message(), this guard also grounds the new test's assertion that get_commit_message was never called.

claims.claim: A focused test for the distinct command/config behavior auto_commits=False was added to TestCoder in tests/basic/test_coder.py, using the same setup/action/assertion discipline as the existing commit-behavior tests (GitTemporaryDirectory, InputOutput, Coder.create with config kwargs, a mock_send edit injector, coder.run, and post-run assertions on file content and commit count).

The asserted behavior is grounded in the coder implementation: auto_commits=False forces dirty_commits=False in Coder.__init__, and Coder.auto_commit short-circuits before repo.commit(), so a GPT SEARCH/REPLACE edit is written to disk while the repository commit count stays at 1 and get_commit_message is never invoked.

conclusion: Added TestCoder.test_auto_commits_disabled_no_commit (tests/basic/test_coder.py:612-663), a focused test for the auto_commits=False coder configuration behavior, written in the same setup/action/assertion discipline as the surrounding commit tests. The test verifies the config wiring (auto_commits False => dirty_commits False), that the mocked GPT edit is still written to disk, and that no commit is created and no commit message is generated. Full pytest execution could not be completed in this environment because GitPython (`import git`) is not installed and dependency installation is out of scope; syntax, AST structure (correct class membership, config kwarg, run call, assertions) and citation line ranges were verified without it.
